name: Map Explainer
look: A continuous top-down satellite world map (deep teal ocean, muted forest green and sand, white ice, soft baked sun, slight vignette and fine grain) with flat saturated colour fills that follow real borders (orange, red, yellow, green, blue), a yellow route line with an end dot, tilted red headline plates and small flat one-hue icons on top.
character: No recurring character: the map is the stage. People appear only as a face in a hexagon badge (about 17% of the width), small flat white pictogram figures (5 at most), or a flat illustrated person cropped at the bottom edge for the closing question.
scenes: One continuous satellite map. One anchor per moment (a filled country, a route, a pin) in the upper two thirds and at most 2 overlays on top, each living 2 s or more and leaving before the next arrives; about one new element per sentence. The camera flies once per change of place and otherwise pushes slowly. One insert (a torn news card) at most.
text: Legion's captions are the ONLY running words: white bold geometric sans, 2-6 words, centred at about 0.70 of the height, key noun or number in yellow. The typed headline bar never repeats the narration: at most a hook title (3-7 words, gone by 4 s) and one chapter word. Number plates hold a number or unit only, tilted on a coloured plate beside what they measure. Place names on the map.
hook: Narration starts at 0.0 s. A tight or bare map with one saturated blob; at 0.25-0.75 s the first noun-graphic lands with a sound hit and the headline types on; by 1-2 s the strange fact and an open question are clear and the camera pulls back. 1-2 camera moves and 8-14 words in the first 3 s. The answer is never named in the hook.
hook_examples: Did you know [place] [one absurd single fact]?
What would happen if [huge physical event] [at a place or for a time]?
What if [one country, continent or resource] [vanished, united or changed]?
Most people have no idea that there was once a real plan to [mega-project] [at a place].
Why the hell is [familiar thing on a map] [odd]?
This man spent [huge number] [extreme act] across [huge scope] with just one rule.
script_rules: Whole channel (809 scripts): the top 20 % run 70-85 s with about 215-235 words in 16-18 sentences of 10-16 words, 2.8-3.1 words per second. Hook sentence about 16 words, one absurd fact or one big what-if, never a list opener ('Here are the...', 'Countries with the most...' lose); the number comes in sentence 2-4, the hook never names the answer. Structure: hook 0-6 s, context 6-18 s (who, where, when, one number), the chain 18-62 s (5-8 steps, each one place or one cause and effect with a number, joined by 'and then', 'but', 'so'), the turn at 62-70 s ('but here's the catch'), and one short last line of 6-14 words after a short pause: an open question to the viewer, a flat final consequence, or the named answer. One place or one number per sentence, plain spoken numbers. No 'subscribe', no 'thanks for watching'. Best themes: world-scale disasters and what-ifs, lost or forbidden places, mega-projects that never happened, choke points, 'why is this country different'. Title = the hook as a question, about 11 words, no emoji, no caps, no hashtags.
pacing: Two thirds of the Short at region or continent zoom, 4-5 zoom levels, none held over 12 s. About one camera move every 4 s (median 18 per Short), 0.4-1.3 s each, ease in and out with the peak at the middle; between two places a fly (zoom out, pan, zoom in, overlapped, 0.7-1.3 s). Every hold keeps a slow push-in (about 6 % a second) plus something moving (a route, a ring pulse, a count). Near-still frames under 20 %, never over 1 s. 0-3 hard cuts (only when the map mode changes), quick dissolves (0.13-0.8 s) only for scale jumps, never a fade to black. Sound hits about 1.2 per second on each graphic's arrival frame, inside words, never on the cut; a quiet whoosh under every fly.
voice: One warm mid-pitched narrator, even and continuous (word gaps near zero, 5-14 pauses of 0.3-0.5 s before turns), -15 LUFS. Light steady music bed 8-14 dB under the voice that dips on pauses. Sound hits are short dry booms, clicks and thumps that mark the arrival of a graphic.
dont: No random gradients, no glow on text (only a thin cyan outline on continents for a world network), no particle bursts, no everything-fades-in, no fake app UI, no two things competing. No hard cuts between places, no black or white fades, no 3D extrusion (a tilted map card on the blue grid is fine, 8-15 degrees, for a hook or the world as an object), no depth of field, no walking or talking characters, no more than 3 fill colours per frame, no fills that ignore real borders, no map rebuilt per scene, no captions under 2 or over 6 words, no answer before the last sentence. No same icon twice in a Short, no more than 4 overlays or 3 stickers at once, no label under 4 % of the width, no zoom past the sharp map. Never a second line of words that repeats the voice; never more than 2 overlays at once; no element that pops in with a bounce or snaps.
